title: Panasonic NN-SF57QSQPQ 27L 1000W Inverter Flatbed Microwave $230 Delivered @ Amazon AU (Price Beat $218.50 @ Officeworks)
body:
Deal: Panasonic NN-SF57QSQPQ 27L 1000W Inverter Flatbed Microwave $230 Delivered @ Amazon AU (Price Beat $218.50 @ Officeworks)

[Commodore64] Flatbed microwaves are so convenient. Also better than the NeoChef that caught fire before it.
[Froot Loops] I've owned 3 of these in 10 years (1 was refurb that broke within 3 years) and one I gave away after ~6 years and I have the latest version now. The latest version with the white LCD screen is a huge improvement on the old greenish screen version (which was already good). These are so easy to clean and cook very good. You can also stick a whole dominos pizza in the box straight in there, so less mess.
[Rimas] We've had the older version of this for close to 5 years now and use it multiple times daily. Good stuff.
[HitlersDad] Forgive the question but does it warm evenly, as it is not moving?
[brimmy11] The heating element moves in the base of the microwave, that's why flatbed microwaves have such a chunky underside.
[PinzVidz] Technically, there is no heating element in a flatbed microwave. It's basically a rotating reflector under the ceramic floor.
[bio] I had one before, and no, it does not warm evenly.
See this: https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/447041#comment-7107334
[mkowarkski] I have this but I feel it is not warming well. For a normal lunch meal (chicken and rice) I have to run it for about 4-5 min. Is it normal or mine is faulty?
[xmail] Extremely bright LED clock that will light your entire house at night.
Does NOT have a plus 10s, plus 1min etc while it is going. You have to clear the time and enter a new time.
Does NOT have a single click "start with 30s" button, you have to enter time and then click start.
[Lancerx] Bugger, that's a deal breaker for me for no 30s increment butting
[xmail] It would take the engineers about 2 minutes of work to add that feature. No idea why they still have something like this in 2026 unless it's intentional to drive people to their more expensive models.
[siuol] Because of no 30s increment I went with Sharp
[oz-dave] It also lacks sensor cooking and relies purely on the timer and/or program mode.
[Pete Gabitas] Looking for a flatbed with a smaller footprint. Any recommendations?
[bleeder] Does this have a reheat button that actually works? Microwave at work has one and it blows my mind how well it works
[Kelvin] These panasonic flatbed microwaves are the worse I have ever used… or had..
I had a cheap Russell Hobb microwave that finally had some intermittent turntable issues (bought as a temporary unit) whilst in a rental… whilst building a house. lasted 7+ years..
So bought the biggest most powerful panasonic flatbed I could get.. biggest mistake.. I knew it straight away after the first use.…. (checking extra carefully through reviews.. it appears common issue with these panansonic microwaves..
takes much longer to heat food up that my previous cheapy… and the food is unevenly heated up as well…
The only good thing is that the flat bed is easier to clean than a normal turnable microwave..
the bell or ding.. also stopped working after a couple of years ..
Also after many years … I still find it hard to get the temps and time right…… often up with a still slight cold soggy food, or piping hot.. slightly dried out mess …
I have reassigned to eating, most of my food slightly cold instead..
I find that using the power setting 3 for 3 minutes .. much more consistent.. than the 30secs - 45 secs on full power… which usually works on all by previous microwaves.. I have owned..
I can't wait for this pile of crap to stop working… so I can buy a different / new microwave…
[tunzafun001] Remember, don't put food near the middle. That is where the reflector is.
This design needs food at the edge … Which is why they are rubbish.
We instinctively chuck items in the middle.
Due to wavelength, it will cook items faster on the outside vs middle as well (hence the inconsistent cooking you mention).
Went back to a 27yr old Sharp… and gave away a 41 year old Sanyo. Still same as day 1
[Bangerbargain] I bought a sharp 32l 1200w, flatbed microwave, its a game changer, heats things up so fast and evenly, the touchscreen display is so easy to use and clean up is a breeze! Havent had any experience with the panasonic flatbeds though.
[oz-dave] I can second that - the Sharp flatbed smart inverter microwave I have is fast and even heating as you say, and so easy to clean.
